strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with interleaved scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 all-reduce operations sequentially, each preceded by local scale application and followed by local scale inversion, exactly as in the reference. 8 all-reduce dispatches with interleaved element-wise operations. Maximizes correctness clarity but high dispatch overhead; no fusion opportunities exploited.

strategies.name: Fused local-ops between collectives
strategies.desc: Merges the scale-divide-scale operations within each stage into single vectorized kernels, reducing memory traffic. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but eliminates redundant clone() and separate loop operations by fusing buf preparation and unscaling into combined kernels. Trades implementation complexity for reduced local memory bandwidth.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction tree
strategies.desc: Exploits the 224-rank world structure (e.g., 28 nodes × 8 devices) by splitting into intra-node reduce-scatter + inter-node all-reduce + intra-node all-gather per stage, then repeating 8 times. Increases total collective count (24 dispatches) but reduces per-dispatch message size and leverages faster intra-node interconnect bandwidth.

strategies.name: Pipelined stage overlapping with async
strategies.desc: Launches all-reduce for stage i+1 on a subset of shards while completing local scaling operations for stage i on other shards, using asynchronous collective calls and tensor chunking. Aims for ~8 dispatches with overlapped compute/communication but requires careful dependency management and may need explicit synchronization barriers.

strategies.name: Batched tensor concatenation approach
strategies.desc:
Precompute all 8 stages' scaling coefficients, stack/concatenate intermediate buffers into a larger tensor, perform fewer (2-3) all-reduce operations on combined payloads with appropriate indexing, then unpack results. Reduces dispatch count to 2-3 but increases per-dispatch payload size by 4-8× and complicates memory layout management.
